findings.title: Template variables are now applied twice in the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before delegating to splitQueriesByStreamShard(), but each shard group is then executed via runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this PR also calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every target again. So in the sharded path every query is interpolated at least twice (once here, and once per shard group inside runSplitQuery — the updated test even asserts applyTemplateVariables was called 5 times for a single query). Beyond the wasted work, double interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent: if a variable's value itself contains a '$'-prefixed token (e.g. a label value like '$foo'), the second pass inside runSplitQuery will re-interpolate it and corrupt the query sent to Loki. Either the interpolation here or in runSplitQuery should be skipped when the queries were already interpolated.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables invoked per shard group via runSplitQuery
findings.body: Because runSplitQuery now unconditionally calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on all targets, the shard-splitting flow (which pre-interpolates in runShardSplitQuery and then calls runSplitQuery once per shard group) re-runs template variable interpolation on every shard sub-request, even though the expressions are already fully interpolated and only differ by the injected __stream_shard__ selector. For dashboards with many template variables this repeats the interpolation/scopedVar resolution work for every shard group; consider interpolating once and passing the results through.
